html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Choose EC2 instance types and placement groups for a workload
  • Configure Auto Scaling with the right metrics and conditions
  • Size Lambda memory and choose between Lambda, Fargate, ECS and EKS
  • Use Batch and EMR for large-scale processing
  • Decouple components so each one scales independently

2Instances, Auto Scaling, serverless and container compute

Running case

Lantern and Loom Handles the Peaks

  • Search traffic doubles every weekend
  • A nightly catalog job crunches numbers for hours
  • Image-resize requests arrive in bursts
  • The data team analyzes terabytes of logs
  • Your job: pick the compute, the size and the scaling rule for each

EC2 Instance Families

Family Optimized for Examples
General purpose A balance of compute, memory and network M, T (burstable)
Compute optimized CPU-bound work: batch, encoding, HPC C
Memory optimized Large in-memory data sets, databases R, X, U
Storage optimized High local disk I/O I, D
Accelerated computing GPUs and AI chips for graphics and machine learning P, G, Inf, Trn
HPC optimized Tightly coupled high-performance computing Hpc
  • T instances earn CPU credits to burst above a baseline
  • A g in the name, such as M7g, means AWS Graviton

Exam tip: Read the bottleneck: CPU, memory, disk or GPU, then pick the family.

Right-Sizing and Placement Groups

  • Right-size: match CPU, memory, network and storage to measured use, and revisit it
  • Graviton (Arm) instances often give better price-performance
  • Cluster placement group: packs instances close together in one AZ for low-latency, high-throughput networking
  • Partition placement group: spreads groups across separate hardware, for Hadoop, Cassandra and Kafka
  • Spread placement group: puts a small group on distinct hardware to limit correlated failure
  • Placement groups are optional and free

Exam tip: Lowest latency between nodes: cluster. Fewest shared failures: spread or partition.

EC2 Auto Scaling Groups

  • A group of instances with a minimum, desired and maximum size
  • A launch template defines what to launch
  • Instances are balanced across AZs and registered with the load balancer automatically
  • Health checks replace unhealthy instances to keep the desired capacity
  • Mix On-Demand and Spot instances; instance refresh rolls out new AMIs
  • No extra charge

Exam tip: Self-healing and elastic fleet: an Auto Scaling group across zones behind a load balancer.

Scaling Policies

Method How it works Use it when
Manual You change the desired capacity Occasional, simple changes
Scheduled Actions run at set dates and times The timing is predictable
Target tracking Hold a metric at a target, like a thermostat Most dynamic workloads
Step and simple Respond to alarm thresholds with set steps You want finer control
Predictive Forecast from history and scale ahead Cyclical traffic, slow start-up
  • Predictive plus dynamic scaling together scales faster than either alone

Exam tip: Hold average CPU near a value: target tracking. Known daily peak: scheduled or predictive.

Metrics and Conditions for Scaling

  • Predefined target tracking metrics: average CPU, network in and out, ALB requests per target
  • EC2 metrics arrive every 5 minutes; turn on detailed monitoring for 1 minute
  • Memory and disk need the CloudWatch agent
  • The metric must rise and fall with the number of instances
  • For queues, track a backlog per instance metric, not the raw queue length
  • Set an instance warmup so new instances are not counted early

Exam tip: Choose a metric that grows when load grows and shrinks when you add instances.

Application Auto Scaling and Scaling Plans Old name [Verify live]

  • Application Auto Scaling scales other resources with the same policy types: ECS service task counts, DynamoDB capacity, Aurora replicas, Lambda provisioned concurrency, Spot Fleet
  • The older AWS Auto Scaling console feature, with scaling plans, ties several resources together
  • The docs now explain how to migrate scaling plans to EC2 Auto Scaling and Application Auto Scaling policies
  • As of 5 November 2026: check how the exam names this feature

Exam tip: Scaling a resource other than EC2? Think Application Auto Scaling policies.

Serverless and Container Compute

Service Sizing and scaling
Lambda Memory 128 MB to 10,240 MB; CPU grows with memory (about one vCPU at 1,769 MB); 15-minute limit; scales by concurrency
Fargate Pick CPU and memory per task; no servers to manage
Amazon ECS Service auto scaling adds or removes tasks; cluster auto scaling adds instances
Amazon EKS Kubernetes scaling on managed nodes, Fargate or Auto Mode
Amazon ECR A private registry for images, with scanning and replication
  • Find the right Lambda memory with monitoring, Power Tuning or Compute Optimizer

Exam tip: A slow CPU-bound Lambda function often needs more memory, which brings more CPU.

3Batch, EMR, decoupling, the design check and practice

AWS Batch and Amazon EMR

Service What it does Choose it for
AWS Batch Runs batch jobs at any scale: you submit jobs to a queue, it provisions EC2, Spot or Fargate capacity Thousands of independent jobs, simulations, rendering
Amazon EMR A managed big data platform for Hadoop, Spark and related frameworks, on EC2, EKS or serverless Large-scale data processing, analytics, ETL
  • Both remove cluster management and scale to the job
  • Use Spot capacity for fault-tolerant batch work

Exam tip: Queue of containerized jobs: Batch. Spark or Hadoop analytics: EMR.

Decoupling and Distributed Compute

  • Decouple with SQS, SNS and EventBridge so producers and consumers scale independently
  • Scale consumers on queue backlog, not on the producers
  • Put compute close to users with multiple Regions and AZs
  • CloudFront moves content and edge logic near users (module 9)
  • Local Zones, Wavelength and Outposts bring compute close to cities, 5G networks and on-premises sites (module 12)
  • Fan out work with Lambda, Step Functions Map or Batch

Exam tip: If one part must scale on its own, put a queue or topic in front of it.

Choosing Compute

Need Choice
Full control, special hardware EC2 with the right family
Elastic fleet of servers EC2 Auto Scaling behind a load balancer
Short, event-driven code Lambda
Containers, no servers Fargate on ECS or EKS
Kubernetes EKS
Queued batch jobs AWS Batch
Spark and Hadoop Amazon EMR
Tightly coupled HPC HPC family in a cluster placement group

Exam tip: Match the unit of work: server, function, container, job or cluster.

What the Exam Asks: High-Performing Compute

  • Which family: instance family or placement group
  • Which scaling: method and metric
  • Which size: instance size, Lambda memory or task size
  • Which service: EC2, Lambda, Fargate, Batch or EMR
  • Which decoupling: the service that lets a tier scale alone

Exam tip: Underline the bottleneck and the shape of the load before choosing.

Design Check: Lantern and Loom Handles the Peaks

Requirement Design
Search traffic doubles each weekend Auto Scaling with target tracking on request count per target
A known Friday evening peak Scheduled or predictive scaling
Order workers fall behind Scale on queue backlog per instance
Image resizing in bursts Lambda, with memory tuned for speed
A nightly job of thousands of tasks AWS Batch with Spot capacity
Terabytes of logs to analyze Amazon EMR
An in-memory search index Memory optimized instances
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Lantern and Loom runs an in-memory product search index that needs a very large amount of memory for each vCPU. Which EC2 instance family fits best?

  • AMemory optimized
  • BCompute optimized
  • CStorage optimized
  • DAccelerated computing
Show the answer

Answer: A. Memory optimized instances provide a high amount of memory for each vCPU for large in-memory data sets. Compute optimized suits CPU-bound work, storage optimized suits local disk I/O, and accelerated computing suits GPU work.

S2The web fleet of Lantern and Loom should keep average CPU utilization near 50 percent as traffic changes, with no manual action. Which scaling approach fits?

  • AManual scaling of the desired capacity
  • BA fixed number of instances, replaced if unhealthy
  • CA target tracking scaling policy on average CPU utilization
  • DA scheduled action that runs once a day
Show the answer

Answer: C. Target tracking holds a metric near a target value by adding and removing instances automatically. Manual and fixed sizes do not react, and a single daily schedule cannot follow changing traffic.

S3Workers in an Auto Scaling group process messages from an Amazon SQS queue. The team wants the worker count to follow the backlog. Which approach works best?

  • ATarget tracking directly on the raw number of visible messages in the queue
  • BTarget tracking on a custom metric of messages per worker instance
  • CTarget tracking on the load balancer request count
  • DScale on the memory of the queue
Show the answer

Answer: B. A scaling metric must rise and fall in proportion to the number of instances, and the raw queue length does not. A backlog-per-instance metric, the queue length divided by the number of workers, does.

S4Which TWO statements about AWS Lambda memory configuration are correct? (Select TWO.)

  • ACPU power is allocated in proportion to the configured memory
  • BMemory is fixed at 128 MB for every function
  • CRaising the memory of a CPU-bound function can shorten its run time
  • DThe maximum memory setting is 3,008 MB
  • EA function can run for up to 60 minutes with the default settings
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Lambda gives more CPU as memory grows, so a CPU-bound function can finish faster. Memory is configurable from 128 MB to 10,240 MB, and the standard invocation limit is 15 minutes.

S5Every night Lantern and Loom must run thousands of independent containerized jobs. It wants a queue, automatic provisioning of cheap Spot capacity, and no cluster to manage. Which service fits?

  • AAmazon EMR with a permanent cluster
  • BAn EC2 Auto Scaling group with manual job scripts
  • CAWS Elastic Beanstalk with a worker environment
  • DAWS Batch
Show the answer

Answer: D. Batch accepts jobs into queues and provisions EC2, Spot or Fargate capacity to run them without cluster management. EMR targets Spark and Hadoop, and the other options leave the scheduling to you.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Instances pick the family by bottleneck; cluster, partition or spread placement
Scaling target tracking for most; scheduled and predictive for known patterns; metrics must track load
Serverless and containers size Lambda memory, use Fargate, ECS or EKS
Big jobs Batch for queued jobs, EMR for Spark and Hadoop
Decouple queues let each part scale alone
